title.zh: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十五: 孝友二
title.en: Volume 198 Biographies 85: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1
title.raw: 卷一百九十八 列傳第八十五: 孝友二 Volume 198 Biographies 85: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1

sentences.zh: 王庸，字伯常，雄州歸信人。

translations.literal: Wang Yong, styled Bochang, was a native of Guixin in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong, whose style was Bochang, came from Guixin in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 事母李氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: He served his mother, Lady Li, and was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother, Lady Li, and his devotion earned wide renown.

sentences.zh: 母有疾，庸夜禱北辰，至叩頭出血，母疾遂愈。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Yong prayed at night to the North Star until his forehead bled from prostration; his mother's illness then abated.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew sick, Yong spent the nights praying to the Pole Star until his forehead bled from bowing; her illness then lifted.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，哀毀幾絕，露處墓前，旦夕悲號。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief and emaciation nearly killed him; he lived in the open before the tomb, wailing morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, grief and wasting nearly took his life; he kept vigil un sheltered before the grave, mourning from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 一夕，雷雨暴至，鄰人持寢席往，欲蔽之，見庸所坐臥之地獨不沾濕，咸嘆異而去。

translations.literal: One night a violent thunderstorm burst upon him; neighbors brought bedding to shelter him, but saw that the ground where Yong sat and lay alone remained dry, and all marveled and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: One night a sudden thunderstorm broke over him; neighbors brought bedding to cover him, yet the spot where Yong sat and slept alone stayed dry while everything around was soaked. They marveled and left.

sentences.zh: 復有蜜蜂數十房，來止其家，歲得蜜蠟，以供祭祀。

translations.literal: Moreover, several dozen beehives came to settle at his home; each year wax and honey were obtained to supply sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Bees also built several dozen hives at his home, and each year the wax and honey they yielded went to his ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 黃贇，字止敬，臨江人。

translations.literal: Huang Yun, styled Zhijing, was a native of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yun, styled Zhijing, came from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 父君道，延祐間求官京師，留贇江南。

translations.literal: His father Jundao, during the Yanyou era, sought office in the capital and left Yun in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jundao went to the capital during the Yanyou period to seek an appointment, leaving Yun behind in the south.

sentences.zh: 時贇年幼，及既長，聞其父娶後妻居永平，乃往省之，則父歿已三年矣。

translations.literal: At that time Yun was young; when he had grown up, hearing his father had taken a second wife and lived at Yongping, he went to visit him, only to find his father had been dead three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was still a child then. When he came of age and learned that his father had remarried and was living at Yongping, he set out to visit him—only to find his father had been dead three years already.

sentences.zh: 庶母聞贇來，盡挾其貲去，更嫁，拒不見贇。

translations.literal: The stepmother, hearing Yun had come, took all the property and left to remarry, refusing to see Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When the stepmother heard Yun had arrived, she seized everything of value, remarried elsewhere, and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 贇號哭語人曰：「吾之來，為省吾父也。

translations.literal: Yun wailed and told people: "I came to visit my father.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wept aloud and told those around him: "I came here to see my father.

sentences.zh: 今不幸吾父已歿，思奉其柩歸而窆之，莫知其墓。

translations.literal: Now, unluckily, my father is already dead; I wish to escort his coffin home for burial but do not know his grave.
translations.idiomatic: Now, alas, he is gone. I long to bring his coffin home for burial, but I do not know where he lies.

sentences.zh: 苟得見庶母示以葬所，死不恨矣，尚忍利遺財邪！

translations.literal: If I could see the stepmother and she showed me the burial place, I would die without regret—how could I yet bear to profit from leftover wealth!
translations.idiomatic: If only she would show me the grave, I could die content. How could I still covet whatever wealth he left behind!

sentences.zh: 」久之，聞庶母居海濱，亟裹糧往。

translations.literal: " After a long while, hearing the stepmother lived by the seashore, he hastily packed provisions and went.
translations.idiomatic: " After some time he learned she was living on the coast, packed food at once, and set out.

sentences.zh: 庶母复拒之，三日不納。

translations.literal: The stepmother again refused him; for three days she would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: She turned him away again and would not let him in for three days.

sentences.zh: 庶母之弟憐之，與偕至永平屬縣樂亭求父墓，又弗得。

translations.literal: The stepmother's younger brother pitied him and went with him to Leting, a subordinate county of Yongping, to seek the father's tomb, but again could not find it.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother took pity on him and went with him to Leting, a county under Yongping, to search for the grave, but they still could not find it.

sentences.zh: 贇哭禱於神，一夕夢老父以杖指葬處曰：「見片磚即可得。

translations.literal: Yun wept and prayed to the spirits; one night he dreamed his aged father pointing with a staff at the burial spot, saying: "When you see a fragment of brick you may obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wept and prayed to the spirits. One night he dreamed of his aged father pointing with a staff at a burial spot and saying: "When you see a broken tile, you will have found it.

sentences.zh: 明日就其地求之，庶母之弟曰：「真是已，斂時有某物可驗。

translations.literal: The next day he sought at that place; the stepmother's younger brother said: "This is truly it; at the encoffining there was a certain object for verification.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he searched there. Her brother said: "This must be it—there was a particular object placed in the coffin when he was buried, by which we can be sure.

sentences.zh: 」啟朽棺，得父骨以歸。

translations.literal: " They opened the decayed coffin and obtained the father's bones to return.
translations.idiomatic: " They opened the rotted coffin, took up his father's bones, and carried them home.

sentences.zh: 石明三者，與母居餘姚山中。

translations.literal: Shi Mingsan lived with his mother in the mountains of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Mingsan and his mother lived in the hills of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 一日明三自外歸，覓母不見，見壁穿而臥內有三虎子，知母為虎所害。

translations.literal: One day Mingsan returned from outside, sought his mother and did not find her; he saw a hole in the wall and within the den three tiger cubs, and knew his mother had been killed by a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: One day he came back from outside and could not find her. He saw a breach in the wall and, inside the lair, three cubs—then knew a tiger had killed his mother.

sentences.zh: 乃盡殺虎子，礪巨斧立壁側，伺母虎至，斫其腦裂而死。

translations.literal: He then killed all the cubs, sharpened a great axe and stood by the wall, waited for the mother tiger to come, and hacked open its skull, splitting it dead.
translations.idiomatic: He killed every cub, sharpened a heavy axe, and stood by the wall until the mother tiger returned; he split its skull and killed it.

sentences.zh: 復往倚岩石傍，執斧伺候，斫殺牡虎。

translations.literal: He again went to lean by the rock side, grasped the axe and waited, and hacked dead the male tiger.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to wait beside the rocks, axe in hand, and struck down the male tiger as well.

sentences.zh: 明三亦立死不僕，張目如生，所執斧牢不可拔。

translations.literal: Mingsan also stood dead without falling; his eyes were open as if alive, and the axe he held could not be pulled free.
translations.idiomatic: Mingsan too stood there dead without collapsing, eyes wide as in life, and the axe in his grip could not be pulled loose.

sentences.zh: 劉琦，岳州臨湘人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi was a native of Linxiang in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi came from Linxiang in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 生二歲而母劉氏遭亂陷於兵，琦獨事其父。

translations.literal: At age two his mother, the Lady Liu, was caught in the chaos of war by soldiers; Qi alone attended his father.
translations.idiomatic: When he was two, his mother, Lady Liu, was swept up in the warfare; Qi grew up attending only his father.

sentences.zh: 稍長，思其母不置，常歎曰：「人皆有母，而我獨無！

translations.literal: When somewhat grown, he could not stop thinking of his mother, and often sighed: "Everyone has a mother, but I alone have none!
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, he could not put his mother out of mind and would often sigh: "Every man has a mother—why do I alone have none!

sentences.zh: 」輒歔欷泣下。

translations.literal: " Then he would sigh and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Then he would sigh and shed tears.

sentences.zh: 及冠，請於父，往求其母。

translations.literal: At coming of age he requested of his father permission to go seek his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached manhood he asked his father's leave to go find her.

sentences.zh: 遍歷河之南北、淮之東西，數歲不得。

translations.literal: He traversed north and south of the River and east and west of the Huai, for several years without finding her.
translations.idiomatic: He searched north and south of the Yellow River and east and west along the Huai for years without success.

sentences.zh: 後求得於池州之貴池，迎以歸養。

translations.literal: Later he found her at Guichi in Chizhou and brought her home to support.
translations.idiomatic: He finally found her at Guichi in Chizhou and brought her home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 其後十五年而父歿，又三年而母歿，終喪猶蔬食。

translations.literal: Afterward fifteen years passed and his father died; three more years and his mother died; through the mourning period he still ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later his father died; three years after that his mother died. He kept to a plain vegetarian diet through the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，旌表其門曰「孝義」。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the matter and awarded his gate the plaque "Filial and Righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his conduct to the court, which honored his household with the inscription "Filial and Righteous."

sentences.zh: 劉源，歸德中牟人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan was a native of Zhongmou in Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan came from Zhongmou in Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母吳氏，年七十餘，病甚不能行。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Wu, was over seventy and seriously ill, unable to walk.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wu, was past seventy, gravely ill, and unable to walk.

sentences.zh: 適兵火起，且延至其家，鄰里俱逃，源力不能救，乃呼天號泣，趨入抱母，為火所焚而死。

translations.literal: Just as military fires rose and spread to their home, all neighbors fled; Yuan had no strength to save them, so he cried to Heaven and rushed in embracing his mother, and was burned to death by the fire.
translations.idiomatic: War fires broke out and soon reached their door; neighbors all fled. Yuan could not rescue her, so he cried to Heaven, ran in, and embraced his mother—and perished in the flames with her.

sentences.zh: 祝公榮，字大昌，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gongrong, styled Dachang, was a native of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gongrong, styled Dachang, came from Lishui in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 隱居養親，事母甚孝。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion supporting his parents and served his mother with great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement to support his parents and served his mother with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 母歿，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, he observed the mourning rites to the letter.

sentences.zh: 灶突失火，公榮力不能救，乃伏棺悲哭，其火自滅，鄉里異之。

translations.literal: The kitchen chimney caught fire; Gongrong lacked strength to save it, so he prostrated himself on the coffin weeping—the fire extinguished itself, and the village marveled.
translations.idiomatic: A fire broke out at the kitchen chimney; unable to fight it, he lay on the coffin and wept until the flames died away on their own. The whole village was astonished.

sentences.zh: 塑二親像於堂，朝夕事之如事生焉。

translations.literal: He sculpted images of both parents in the hall and morning and evening served them as if they were alive.
translations.idiomatic: He fashioned statues of both parents in the hall and tended them morning and evening as though they were still alive.

sentences.zh: 陸思孝，紹興山陰樵者，性至孝。

translations.literal: Lu Sixiao was a woodcutter of Shanyin in Shaoxing, whose nature was utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sixiao was a woodcutter from Shanyin in Shaoxing, a man of the deepest filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 母老病痢，思孝醫禱久之，不效。

translations.literal: His mother was old and ill with dysentery; Sixiao sought medicine and prayed for a long time without effect.
translations.idiomatic: His aged mother suffered from dysentery. Sixiao sought physicians and prayed for a long time, but nothing helped.

sentences.zh: 思孝方欲刲股肉為糜以進，忽夢寐間怳若有神人者授以藥劑，思孝得而異之，即以奉母，其疾遂愈。

translations.literal: Sixiao was about to cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel to offer, when suddenly in sleep he seemed dimly to have a divine person hand him medicine; Sixiao obtained it and marveled, immediately presented it to his mother, and her illness then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to cut flesh from his thigh to cook gruel for her when, in a dream, a figure like a god handed him a dose of medicine. He gave it to his mother at once, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 姜兼，嚴州淳安人。

translations.literal: Jiang Jian was a native of Chun'an in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jian came from Chun'an in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，與二兄養母至孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers supported their mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, he and his two elder brothers raised their mother with devoted care.

sentences.zh: 母死，兼哀慕幾絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Jian's grief and longing nearly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, Jian's grief nearly destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 既葬，獨居墓下，朝夕哭奠，寂焉荒山中，躬自樵爨，蔬食飲水，一衰麻寒暑不易。

translations.literal: After burial he dwelt alone below the tomb, morning and evening weeping offerings; in silence on the desolate mountain he himself gathered fuel and cooked, ate vegetables and drank water, and one set of mourning clothes he did not change through cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he lived alone at the grave, mourning morning and night on a lonely mountain slope. He gathered his own firewood, cooked for himself, ate only vegetables and drank only water, and wore the same hemp mourning garments through winter and summer alike.

sentences.zh: 同里陳氏、戴氏子不能事其父母，聞兼之行，慚感而悔，皆迎養焉。

translations.literal: Sons of the Chen and Dai families in the same village could not serve their parents; hearing Jian's conduct, they felt ashamed and repented, and all brought their parents home to support.
translations.idiomatic: Young men of the Chen and Dai families nearby had neglected their parents; when they heard of Jian's example they were ashamed, repented, and each brought his parents home to care for them.

sentences.zh: 胡伴侶，鈞州密縣人。

translations.literal: Hu Banlü was a native of Mi County in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Banlü came from Mi County in Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父實嘗患心疾數月，幾死，更數醫俱莫能療。

translations.literal: His father Shi had suffered heart illness for several months, nearly dying; changing physicians all could not cure him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi had suffered a heart ailment for months and was near death; one physician after another failed to cure him.

sentences.zh: 伴侶乃齋沐焚香，泣告於天，以所佩小刀於右脅傍刲其皮膚，割脂一片，煎藥以進，父疾遂瘳，其傷亦旋愈。

translations.literal: Banlü then purified himself and burned incense, weeping to Heaven, took the small knife at his belt and beside his right ribs cut open the skin, cut out a piece of fat, decocted medicine to present, and his father's illness then recovered; his wound also soon healed.
translations.idiomatic: Banlü bathed, burned incense, and wept to Heaven, then took the small knife at his belt, cut the skin beside his right ribs, sliced out a piece of flesh, boiled it into medicine, and gave it to his father, who recovered. His own wound healed quickly as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷旌表其門。

translations.literal: The court awarded and marked his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and marked his gate with an honorific plaque.

sentences.zh: 王士弘，延安中部人。

translations.literal: Wang Shihong was a native of Zhongbu in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihong came from Zhongbu in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 父摶有疾，士弘傾家貲求醫，見醫即拜，遍禱諸神，叩額成瘡。

translations.literal: His father Tuohuo had illness; Shihong exhausted family wealth seeking doctors, bowing whenever he saw a physician, praying to all deities until his forehead became sores.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Tuohuo fell ill, Shihong spent the family fortune on doctors, bowing to every physician he met and praying to every god until his forehead was raw with sores from prostration.

sentences.zh: 父歿，哀毀盡禮，廬墓三年，足未嘗至家。

translations.literal: When his father died, grief and rites were fully observed; he built a hut at the tomb for three years, his feet never having reached home.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning in full and kept a hut by the grave for three years, never once setting foot inside his house.

sentences.zh: 墓廬上有奇鵲來巢，飛鳥翔集，與士弘親近，若相狎然，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: On the tomb hut a strange magpie came to nest; flying birds gathered and drew near Shihong as if familiar, and all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: A remarkable magpie nested on the mourning hut; birds flew down and lingered close to Shihong as if tame, and onlookers were amazed.

sentences.zh: 終喪，復建祠於塋前，朔望必往奠祭，雖風雨不廢也。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again built a shrine before the mound; on the first and fifteenth of each month he invariably went to offer sacrifice, never stopping even in wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he built a shrine before the mound and, on the first and fifteenth of every month, went to offer sacrifice without fail, even in storm and rain.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事於朝，旌表之。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the matter to court and awarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported his conduct, and the court honored him.

sentences.zh: 何從義，延安洛川人。

translations.literal: He Congyi was a native of Luochuan in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He Congyi came from Luochuan in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖良、祖母李氏偕亡，從義廬於墓側，旦夕哀慕，不脫絰帶，不食菜果，惟啖疏食而已。

translations.literal: Grandfather Liang and grandmother the Lady Li died together; Congyi built a hut beside the tomb, morning and evening full of grief, never removing mourning bands, eating no vegetables or fruits, only coarse food.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandfather Liang and grandmother Lady Li died together, Congyi kept a hut by their grave, grieving from dawn to dusk, never removing his mourning sash, eating no vegetables or fruit—only plain grain.

sentences.zh: 事父世榮、母王氏，孝養尤至。

translations.literal: He served father Shirong and mother the Lady Wang with especially complete filial support.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his father Shirong and his mother Lady Wang with still greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 伯祖溫、伯祖母郝氏，叔祖恭、叔祖母賀氏，叔祖讓、叔祖母姜氏，叔父珍、叔母光氏，皆無子。

translations.literal: Great-uncle Wen, great-aunt the Lady Hao, uncle Gong, uncle's wife Lady He, uncle Rang, aunt Lady Jiang, uncle Zhen, uncle's wife Lady Guang—all were without sons.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Wen and great-aunt Lady Hao, uncles Gong and Rang with their wives Ladies He and Jiang, and uncle Zhen and aunt Lady Guang—all were childless.

sentences.zh: 比其亡也，從義咸為治葬，築高墳，祭奠以禮，時人義之。

translations.literal: When each of them died, Congyi all arranged burials, built high mounds, and sacrificed according to rites; people of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When each of them died, Congyi arranged the funeral, raised a high mound, and performed the rites of sacrifice. People praised his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 哈都赤，大都固安州人。

translations.literal: Haduochi was a native of Gu'anzhou near Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Haduochi came from Gu'an Prefecture in the Dadu region.

sentences.zh: 天性篤孝。

translations.literal: His nature was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養母，母嘗有疾，醫治不痊，哈都赤礪其所佩小刀，拜天泣曰：「慈母生我劬勞，今當捐身報之。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he supported his mother; when his mother had illness physicians could not cure it, Haduochi sharpened the small knife he wore, bowed to Heaven weeping: "My loving mother bore me with toil; now I must give my body to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he raised his mother. When she fell ill and doctors could not cure her, Haduochi sharpened the knife at his belt, bowed to Heaven, and wept: "My mother bore me with endless labor; now I must repay her with my own flesh.

sentences.zh: 」乃割開左脅，取肉一片，作羹進母，母曰：「此何肉也？

translations.literal: " He then cut open his left ribs, took a piece of flesh, made broth to present to his mother; mother said: "What flesh is this?
translations.idiomatic: " He cut open his left side, took a slice of flesh, and cooked it into soup for her. His mother asked: "What meat is this?

sentences.zh: 其甘如是！

translations.literal: How sweet it is!
translations.idiomatic: It tastes so sweet!

sentences.zh: 」數日而病癒。

translations.literal: " Within several days the illness recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Within days she was well again.

sentences.zh: 高必達，建昌人。

translations.literal: Gao Bida was a native of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bida came from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 五歲時，父明大忽棄家遠遊，莫知所適。

translations.literal: At age five his father Mingda suddenly abandoned the household and traveled far, none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five, his father Mingda suddenly left home and wandered far away; no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 必達既長，晝夜哀慕，乃娶妻以養母，而歷往四方求其父。

translations.literal: When Bida had grown, day and night grieving, he took a wife to support his mother, and meanwhile went through the four directions seeking his father.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, he mourned his father day and night, took a wife to care for his mother, and traveled in every direction searching for him.

sentences.zh: 十餘年不得見，心愈悲。

translations.literal: After more than ten years without seeing him, his heart grew more sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years passed without a sight of him, and his sorrow only deepened.

sentences.zh: 忽相傳黃州全真道院中有虛明子者，學道三十年矣，本姓高氏，建昌人也，匿姓名為道人云。

translations.literal: Suddenly it was said that at the Quanzhen Daoist abbey in Huangzhou there was one called Master Illuminated Void who had studied the Way thirty years, originally surnamed Gao of Jianchang, concealing his name as a Daoist.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that at the Quanzhen monastery in Huangzhou there lived a recluse called Master Illuminated Void who had cultivated the Way for thirty years—originally a Gao from Jianchang, now hiding his identity as a Daoist.

sentences.zh: 必達詢問，知為父，即往拜之，具言家世，及己之所生歲月，大父母之喪葬始末，因哀號叩頭不已。

translations.literal: Bida inquired and knew it was his father; he immediately went to bow, detailed the family history and his own birth month, the beginning and end of the great-grandparents' burials, and thus wailed and prostrated ceaselessly.
translations.idiomatic: Bida made inquiries, recognized his father, went at once to bow before him, and recited the family history, his own birth date, and every detail of his grandparents' deaths and burials, weeping and kowtowing without cease.

sentences.zh: 虛明猶瞑坐不顧，久之，斥曰：「我非汝父，不去何為？

translations.literal: Illuminated Void still sat with eyes closed and did not regard him; after a long time he rebuked: "I am not your father—why do you not leave?
translations.idiomatic: Illuminated Void kept his eyes closed and ignored him. At last he snapped: "I am not your father. Why will you not go?

sentences.zh: 」必達留侍左右不少懈，辭氣哀惻可矜。

translations.literal: " Bida remained attending at his side without slackening, his words sorrowful enough to pity.
translations.idiomatic: " Bida stayed at his side without rest, his pleas so pitiful they moved everyone who heard.

sentences.zh: 其徒謂虛明曰：「師有子如此，忍弗歸乎？

translations.literal: His disciples said to Illuminated Void: "Master, you have a son such as this—can you bear not to return?
translations.idiomatic: His disciples said: "Master, you have a son like this—how can you refuse to go home?

sentences.zh: 」虛明不得已，乃還家。

translations.literal: " Illuminated Void had no choice and then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " At last Illuminated Void yielded and returned with him.

sentences.zh: 必達孝養篤至，鄉里稱之。

translations.literal: Bida's filial support was deeply complete; the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Bida cared for him with unstinting devotion, and the neighborhood praised them both.

sentences.zh: 曾德，漁陽人，宗聖公五十七代孫。

translations.literal: Zeng De was a native of Yuyang, fifty-seventh-generation descendant of the Duke of the Sage's line.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng De came from Yuyang and was of the fifty-seventh generation after the Duke of the Sage.

sentences.zh: 母早亡，父仲祥再娶左氏。

translations.literal: His mother died early; his father Zhongxiang remarried the Lady Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died young; his father Zhongxiang married again, taking Lady Zuo.

sentences.zh: 仲祥遊襄陽，樂其土俗，因攜左氏家焉。

translations.literal: Zhongxiang traveled to Xiangyang, delighted with its customs, and thus brought the Lady Zuo's household there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang went to Xiangyang, took to the place, and moved Lady Zuo's household there with him.

sentences.zh: 亂兵陷襄陽，遂失左氏。

translations.literal: Rebel soldiers overran Xiangyang and thus the Lady Zuo was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel troops overran the city, Lady Zuo was lost in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 德遍往南土求之，五年乃得於廣海間，奉迎以歸，孝養甚至。

translations.literal: De searched throughout the southern lands; in five years he found her among the Guang sea regions, brought her back with honor, and supported her with extreme filiality.
translations.idiomatic: De searched the south for five years, found her along the Guang coast, brought her home with honor, and cared for her with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，詔旌復其家。

translations.literal: The authorities reported; an edict awarded and restored his household.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the matter, and an imperial edict commended and restored his household.

sentences.zh: 靳昺，字克昌，絳州曲沃人。

translations.literal: Jin Bing, styled Kechang, was a native of Quwo in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Bing, styled Kechang, came from Quwo in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄榮為奎章閣承製學士，奉母王氏官於朝。

translations.literal: Elder brother Rong was academician-attendant of the Kuizhang Pavilion, supporting mother Lady Wang in office at court.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rong served as academician-attendant of the Kuizhang Pavilion and kept their mother Lady Wang with him at court.

sentences.zh: 母歿，昺與兄榮護喪還家。

translations.literal: When mother died, Bing and brother Rong escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, Bing and Rong escorted her coffin home.

sentences.zh: 至平定，大雷雨，流水驟至，昺伏柩上，榮呼之避水，昺不忍捨去，遂為水所漂沒。

translations.literal: Reaching Pingding, great thunder and rain came, flood waters suddenly arrived; Bing lay on the coffin; Rong called him to avoid the water—Bing could not bear to leave and was swept away drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingding a thunderstorm broke and a flash flood rushed in. Bing lay across the coffin; Rong shouted for him to flee, but Bing would not leave his mother and was swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 後得王氏柩於三里外，得昺屍於五里外。

translations.literal: Later Lady Wang's coffin was found three li away, and Bing's corpse five li away.
translations.idiomatic: Her coffin was recovered three li downstream; Bing's body was found five li away.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《孝子靳昺碑》。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the "Stele of the Filial Son Jin Bing."
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the inscription 《Stele of the Filial Son Jin Bing》.

sentences.zh: 黃道賢，泉州人。

translations.literal: Huang Daoxian was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daoxian came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嫡母唐無子，道賢在襁褓而生母蘇以疾去。

translations.literal: The principal mother Tang had no son; Daoxian in swaddling clothes his birth mother Su left due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: His father's principal wife, Lady Tang, had no children of her own; while Daoxian was still in swaddling clothes his birth mother Lady Su left the household because of illness.

sentences.zh: 既長，思念生母，屢請於父，得召之歸。

translations.literal: When grown, longing for his birth mother, he repeatedly requested of his father and was able to summon her back.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, longing for Lady Su, he begged his father again and again until she was brought back.

sentences.zh: 道賢竭力養二母，得其歡心。

translations.literal: Daoxian exerted himself to support both mothers and gained their delight.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to both mothers and won their affection.

sentences.zh: 父病篤，道賢晝夜奉湯藥，不離膝下，遍求良醫，莫效。

translations.literal: When his father was critically ill, Daoxian day and night presented broth and medicine, not leaving his knee; he sought good physicians everywhere without effect.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Daoxian tended him day and night at his bedside, bringing broth and medicine, and sought physicians far and wide, but none could help.

sentences.zh: 乃夜禱於天，願減己一紀之算，以益父壽，其父遂愈。

translations.literal: He then prayed at night to Heaven, wishing to reduce his own life by one cycle to extend his father's lifespan; his father then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to Heaven that his own life might be shortened by one twelve-year cycle in exchange for his father's, and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 至元統二年乃歿，果符一紀之數。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhiyuantong reign he died, indeed matching the one-cycle count.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhiyuantong reign—exactly one cycle later, as he had vowed.

sentences.zh: 道賢居喪盡禮，負土築墳，廬於墓側，疏食終制。

translations.literal: Daoxian observed mourning with full rites, carried earth to build the mound, built a hut beside the tomb, and ate only plain food through the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxian mourned by the book, piled earth on the grave, kept a hut at the tomb, and ate only plain food until the mourning term ended.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，有司上其事，旌其門曰「孝子黃氏之門」。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhiyuan reign, the authorities reported the matter and awarded his gate the inscription "Gate of the Filial Son of the Huang Clan."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan, officials reported his conduct and marked his gate "Gate of the Filial Son of the Huang Clan."

sentences.zh: 史彥斌，邳州人。

translations.literal: Shi Yanbin was a native of Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanbin came from Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜學，有孝行。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had conduct of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to study and renowned for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，河溢，金鄉、魚台墳墓多壞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, the river overflowed and many tombs in Jinxiang and Yutai were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 14 the Yellow River burst its banks, and graves throughout Jinxiang and Yutai were washed away.

sentences.zh: 彥斌母卒，慮有後患，乃為厚棺，刻銘曰「邳州沙河店史彥斌母柩」，仍以四鐵環釘其上，然後葬。

translations.literal: When Yanbin's mother died, fearing later trouble, he made a thick coffin and carved an inscription reading "Coffin of the Mother of Shi Yanbin of Shahedian, Pizhou," still fastening four iron rings on top, and then buried her.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, fearing what the flood might do, Yanbin commissioned a heavy coffin, had it inscribed "Coffin of the Mother of Shi Yanbin of Shahedian, Pizhou," nailed four iron rings to the lid, and buried her.

sentences.zh: 明年，墓果為水所漂，彥斌縛草為人，置水中，仰天呼曰：「母棺被水，不知其處，願天矜憐哀子之心，假此芻靈，指示母棺。

translations.literal: The next year the tomb was indeed swept away by water; Yanbin bound straw into a human figure, placed it in the water, and cried to Heaven: "My mother's coffin has been taken by the water and I do not know where it is. May Heaven pity a grieving son's heart and lend this straw effigy to point me to my mother's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the grave was carried off by the flood. Yanbin fashioned a straw figure, set it afloat, and cried to Heaven: "My mother's coffin is lost in the waters. Pity a son's grief, and let this straw proxy show me where she lies.

sentences.zh: 」言訖，涕泣橫流，乃乘舟隨草人所之。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking, tears streamed across his face; he then took a boat and followed wherever the straw figure went.
translations.idiomatic: " Weeping, he boarded a boat and followed the figure downstream.

sentences.zh: 經十餘日，行三百餘里，草人止桑林中，視之，母柩在焉，載歸复葬之。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, traveling over three hundred li, the straw figure stopped in a mulberry grove; looking, the mother's coffin was there; he loaded it and returned to rebury it.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten days he traveled over three hundred li until the figure halted in a mulberry grove—and there was his mother's coffin. He brought it home and buried her again.

sentences.zh: 張紹祖，字子讓，潁州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shaozu, styled Zirang, was a native of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaozu, styled Zirang, came from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 讀書力學，以孝行聞於朝，特授河南路儒學教授。

translations.literal: He read books and studied diligently; his filial conduct was heard at court, and he was specially appointed professor of the Henan Circuit Confucian school.
translations.idiomatic: A serious scholar known for filial piety, he was specially appointed professor at the Henan Circuit Confucian school.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，奉父避兵山間，賊至，執其父將殺之，紹祖泣曰：「吾父耆德善人，不當害，請殺我以代父死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng, he led his father to escape warfare in the mountains; bandits arrived, seized his father and were about to kill him; Shaozu wept saying: "My father is an aged man of virtue and goodness and ought not be harmed—please kill me in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 15 he took his father into the hills to escape the fighting. When bandits seized his father and raised their blades, Shaozu wept: "My father is an old man of virtue. Do not harm him—kill me instead.

sentences.zh: 且若等非父母所生乎，何忍害人父也！

translations.literal: Moreover are you not also born of parents—how can you bear to harm another's father!
translations.idiomatic: Were you not born of parents yourselves? How can you bear to kill another man's father!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，以戈擊之，戈應手挫鈍，因感而相謂曰：「此真孝子，不可害。

translations.literal: " The bandits were angry and struck him with a spear; the spear's edge dulled in their hands; moved, they said to one another: "This is a true filial son and must not be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits struck him with a spear, but the blade turned blunt in their hands. Moved, they said to one another: "This is a true filial son—we must not harm him.

sentences.zh: 」乃釋之。

translations.literal: " and then released them.
translations.idiomatic: They released them.

sentences.zh: 李明德，瑞州路上高縣人。

translations.literal: Li Mingde was a native of Shanggao County in Ruizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mingde came from Shanggao in Ruizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 讀書有志操，孝行篤至。

translations.literal: He read books with firm resolve and conduct of filial piety that was deeply complete.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of learning and principle, whose filial devotion was unwavering.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，亂兵陷袁州，因抄掠上高。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, rebel soldiers overran Yuanzhou and thus raided Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 14 rebel troops took Yuanzhou and swept through Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 兵執其父欲殺之，明德泣告曰：「子豈不能代父乎，願勿害吾父也！

translations.literal: Soldiers seized his father intending to kill him; Mingde wept and pleaded: "Can a son not take his father's place—please do not harm my father!
translations.idiomatic: They seized his father to kill him. Mingde wept and pleaded: "Let me die in his place—spare my father!

sentences.zh: 」兵遂殺明德，而免其父，後以高壽終。

translations.literal: " The soldiers then killed Mingde and spared his father, who later died at a great age.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers killed Mingde and spared his father, who lived to a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 張緝，字士明，益都膠州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Shiming, was a native of Jiaozhou in Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Shiming, came from Jiaozhou in Yidu.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，能詩文。

translations.literal: His nature was filial and brotherly; he could compose poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his parents and devoted to his brothers, and wrote poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，與兄紳、弟經同領鄉薦，由澤州儒學正轉泰州幕職，棄之，養親居揚州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng, he and elder brother Shen and younger brother Jing together received provincial recommendation; from director of the Zezhou Confucian school he was transferred to a post on the Taizhou staff, which he abandoned to support his parents and live at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 7 he and his brothers Shen and Jing passed the provincial examination together. He served as director of the Zezhou school, then took a post on the Taizhou staff—but gave it up to care for his parents in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，揚州亂，緝母姬氏方臥病，賊突入臥內，舉槍欲刺姬，緝以身蔽姬，槍中緝脅，三日而死。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yangzhou fell into chaos; Ji's mother the Lady Ji was lying ill; bandits burst into the bedchamber and raised a spear intending to stab Ji; Ji used his body to shield the Lady Ji; the spear struck Ji's ribs and after three days he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Yangzhou erupted in violence. His mother Lady Ji lay ill in bed when bandits burst in and leveled a spear at her. Ji threw himself across her body; the spear pierced his ribs, and he died three days later.

sentences.zh: 魏敬益，字士友，雄州容城人。

translations.literal: Wei Jingyi, styled Shiyou, was a native of Rongcheng in Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingyi, styled Shiyou, came from Rongcheng in Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，居母喪，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; dwelling in his mother's mourning, grief and emaciation left only skin on bone.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he mourned his mother until grief had worn him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 素好施與​​，有男女失時者，出貲財為之嫁娶；

translations.literal: He had always loved giving; for men and women who had missed their season for marriage, he provided funds to marry them off;
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by habit: when men or women had no means to marry, he supplied the dowry or bride-price;

sentences.zh: 歲凶，老弱之飢者，為糜以食之。

translations.literal: in years of famine, for the old and weak who were hungry, he made gruel to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: in famine years he cooked gruel for the elderly and the weak who had nothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 敬益有田僅十六頃，一日語其子曰：「自吾買四莊村之田十頃，環其村之民皆不能自給，吾深憫焉。

translations.literal: Jingyi had only sixteen qing of fields; one day he told his sons: "Since I bought the ten qing of fields at Sizhuang Village, the villagers all around cannot support themselves—I deeply pity them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi owned only sixteen qing of land. One day he told his sons: "When I bought the ten qing at Sizhuang Village, the farmers there could no longer make a living. I have pitied them ever since.

sentences.zh: 今將以田歸其人，汝謹守餘田，可無餒也。

translations.literal: Now I will return the fields to the people; you carefully keep the remaining fields and you will not go hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Today I mean to give those fields back. Guard the rest carefully and you will not want for food.

sentences.zh: 」乃呼四莊村民諭之曰：「吾買若等業，使若等貧不聊生，有親無以養，吾之不仁甚​​矣，請以田歸若等。

translations.literal: " He then called the villagers of the four villages and told them: "I bought your livelihoods and made you so poor you cannot get by, with parents you cannot support—my lack of benevolence is very great; please take back your fields.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned the villagers and said: "I bought your land and left you destitute, unable even to support your parents. That was a grave wrong. Take the fields back.

sentences.zh: 」眾聞，皆愕眙不敢受，強與之，乃受而言諸有司。

translations.literal: " When all heard this they were stunned and dared not accept; he forced it on them and they then accepted and reported to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: " They were astonished and refused at first, but he pressed them until they accepted, then reported the gift to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞於中書，請加旌表。

translations.literal: The authorities reported to the Central Secretariat, requesting additional commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials forwarded the matter to the Central Secretariat, asking that he be specially honored.

sentences.zh: 丞相賀太平歎曰：「世乃有斯人哉！」

translations.literal: Chief Councillor He Taiding sighed: "Can there truly be such a man in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor He Taiding exclaimed: "That such a man exists in our age!"

sentences.zh: 湯霖，字伯雨，龍興新建人。

translations.literal: Tang Lin, styled Boyu, was a native of Xinjian in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin, styled Boyu, came from Xinjian in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，事母至孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father died while he was young; he cared for his mother with the deepest devotion.

sentences.zh: 母嘗病熱，更數醫弗能效。

translations.literal: His mother once had feverish illness; changing physicians all could not cure it.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill with fever, physician after physician failed to help.

sentences.zh: 母不肯飲藥，曰：「惟得冰，我疾乃可愈。

translations.literal: His mother would not drink medicine, saying: "Only if I obtain ice can my illness then be cured.
translations.idiomatic: She would not take their prescriptions and said: "Only ice can cure me.

sentences.zh: 」爾時天氣甚燠，霖求冰不得，累日號哭於池上。

translations.literal: " At that time the weather was very hot; Lin sought ice but could not obtain it, and for many days wailed by the pool.
translations.idiomatic: " It was the height of summer. Lin searched in vain for ice and for days wept beside a pond.

sentences.zh: 忽聞池中戛戛有聲，拭淚視之，乃冰澌也。

translations.literal: Suddenly he heard a crackling sound in the pool; wiping his tears and looking, it was ice forming.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he heard ice cracking in the pond. He wiped his eyes—and saw ice forming.

sentences.zh: 亟取以奉母，其疾果愈。

translations.literal: He immediately took it to present to his mother; her illness indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered it at once for his mother, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 孫抑，字希武，世居晉寧洪洞縣。

translations.literal: Sun Yi, styled Xiwu, had his family dwelling for generations in Hongdong County in Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Xiwu, came from a family long settled in Hongdong, Jinning.

sentences.zh: 抑登進士第，歷仕至刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in office reaching director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 關保之變，挈父母妻子避兵平陽之柏村。

translations.literal: At the Guanbao rebellion he took parents, wife, and children to escape warfare to Baicun in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guanbao uprising broke out, he fled with his parents, wife, and children to Baicun in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 有亂兵至村剽掠，拔白刃嚇抑母，求財不得，舉刃欲斫之。

translations.literal: Rebel soldiers came to the village to plunder; drawing bare blades they terrified Yi's mother, seeking wealth but obtaining none, and raised the blade intending to hack her.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops raided the village. They brandished swords at Yi's mother, demanded money, found none, and raised a blade to strike her down.

sentences.zh: 抑亟以身蔽母，請代受斫，母乃得釋。

translations.literal: Yi urgently used his body to shield his mother, requesting to receive the hacking in her stead; his mother was thus released.
translations.idiomatic: Yi threw himself in front of her and begged to take the blow himself. His mother was spared.

sentences.zh: 而抑父被虜去，不知所之。

translations.literal: But Yi's father was captured and taken away, none knew where.
translations.idiomatic: His father, however, was seized and carried off—no one knew where.

sentences.zh: 或語之曰：「汝父被驅而東矣，然東軍得所掠民皆殺之，汝慎無往就死也。

translations.literal: Someone told him: "Your father was driven eastward; yet the eastern army kills all civilians they seize—you must be careful not to go and die.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: "They drove your father east. The eastern army kills every captive it takes—do not throw your life away.

sentences.zh: 」抑曰：「吾可畏死而棄吾父乎？

translations.literal: " Yi said: "How can I fear death and abandon my father?
translations.idiomatic: " Yi replied: "How can I fear death and abandon my father?

sentences.zh: 」遂往，出入死地，屢瀕危殆，卒得父以歸。

translations.literal: " He then went, entering and leaving the land of death, several times on the brink of peril, and finally obtained his father and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He set out, passed again and again through mortal danger, and at last brought his father home.

sentences.zh: 石永，紹興新昌人。

translations.literal: Shi Yong was a native of Xinchang in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yong came from Xinchang in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 性淳厚，事親至孝。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and thick; he served his parents with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and steadfast by nature, he served his parents with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 值亂兵掠鄉里，永父謙孫年八十，老不能行，永負父匿山谷中。

translations.literal: When rebel soldiers plundered the village, Yong's father Qiansun was eighty and old, unable to walk; Yong carried his father and hid in a mountain valley.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits swept the countryside, Yong's father Qiansun was eighty and could not walk. Yong carried him into the hills to hide.

sentences.zh: 亂兵執其父，欲殺之，永亟前抱父請以身代，兵遂殺永而釋其父。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers seized his father intending to kill him; Yong urgently went forward embracing his father and requested to use his body in substitution; the soldiers then killed Yong and released his father.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the old man to kill him. Yong rushed forward, embraced his father, and begged to die in his place. The soldiers killed Yong and let his father go.

sentences.zh: 王克己，延安中部人。

translations.literal: Wang Keji was a native of Zhongbu in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Keji came from Zhongbu in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 父伯通歿，克己負土築墳，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: When father Botong died, Keji carried earth to build the mound and built a hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After his father Botong died, Keji piled earth on the grave and kept a mourning hut beside it.

sentences.zh: 貊高縱兵暴掠，縣民皆逃竄，克己獨守墓不去。

translations.literal: Mo Gao's soldiers violently plundered; county people all fled, but Keji alone guarded the tomb and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Gao's troops ravaged the district, everyone fled—yet Keji alone stayed at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 家人呼之避兵，克己曰：「吾誓守墓三年，以報吾親，雖死不可棄也。

translations.literal: Family called him to avoid the soldiers; Keji said: "I have sworn to guard the tomb three years to repay my parents—even in death I cannot abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: His kin urged him to run. Keji said: "I vowed to keep vigil at this grave for three years to repay my parents. I will not leave, even if it costs my life.

sentences.zh: 」遂不去。

translations.literal: " and then did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He would not leave.

sentences.zh: 俄而兵至，見其身衣衰絰，形容憔悴，曰：「此孝子也！

translations.literal: Shortly soldiers arrived; seeing him wearing hemp mourning garments, his appearance haggard, they said: "This is a filial son!
translations.idiomatic: Soon the soldiers came. Seeing him in hemp mourning clothes, wasted and worn, they said: "This is a filial son!

sentences.zh: 」遂不忍害，竟終喪而歸。

translations.literal: " and then could not bear to harm him, and in the end he completed mourning and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " They would not harm him. He finished the mourning period and went home.

sentences.zh: 劉思敬，延安宜君人。

translations.literal: Liu Sijing was a native of Yijun in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sijing came from Yijun in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 事其繼母沙氏、杜氏，孝養之至，無異親母。

translations.literal: He served his stepmothers the Lady Sha and the Lady Du with filial support to the utmost, no different from birth mothers.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his stepmothers Lady Sha and Lady Du as devotedly as if they were his own mothers.

sentences.zh: 父年八十，兩目俱喪明，會亂兵剽掠其鄉，思敬負父避於巖穴中。

translations.literal: His father was eighty and both eyes had lost sight; when rebel soldiers plundered their village, Sijing carried his father to hide in a rock cave.
translations.idiomatic: His father was eighty and blind when rebel troops overran the countryside. Sijing carried him into a cave in the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 有兵至，欲殺思敬，思敬泣言曰：「我父老矣，又無目，我死不足惜，使我父何依乎？

translations.literal: Soldiers came intending to kill Sijing; Sijing wept saying: "My father is old, and moreover without eyes; my death is not worth regretting—but what would my father rely on?
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers came to kill him. Sijing wept: "My father is old and sightless. My death means little—but what would become of him?

sentences.zh: 」兵憐其孝，不忍殺，父子皆免於難。

translations.literal: " The soldiers pitied his filial piety and could not bear to kill; father and son both escaped the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " They pitied his devotion and spared them both.

sentences.zh: 呂祐，字伯通，晉安人。

translations.literal: Lü You, styled Botong, was a native of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lü You, styled Botong, came from Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 至正二十六年，郡城破，有卒入其室，拔白刃脅其母林氏索財寶不得，揮刃欲斫母。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Zhizheng the prefectural city fell; a soldier entered his chamber, drew a bare blade and threatened his mother the Lady Lin seeking treasure but obtaining none, and waved the blade intending to hack the mother.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 26 the prefectural city fell. A soldier entered his home, drew a sword, and threatened his mother Lady Lin for valuables. Finding none, he raised the blade to strike her.

sentences.zh: 祐急以身蔽母，而奪其刃，手指盡裂，被傷僕地。

translations.literal: You urgently used his body to shield his mother and seized the blade; his fingers were all split, and he was wounded and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: You threw himself between them, wrested the blade away, and had every finger split open before he collapsed, wounded.

sentences.zh: 良久而蘇，開目視母曰：「母幸無恙，我死無憾矣。

translations.literal: After a long while he revived, opened his eyes and looked at his mother saying: "Mother is fortunately unharmed; I die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he came to and, opening his eyes, looked at his mother: "You are safe—that is enough. I die content.

sentences.zh: 」遂瞑目死。

translations.literal: " and then closed his eyes and died.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his eyes and died.

sentences.zh: 周樂，溫州瑞安人。

translations.literal: Zhou Le was a native of Ruian in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Le came from Ruian in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋狀元坦之後，父日成，通經能文。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Song zhuangyuan Zhou Tan, his father Richeng was versed in the classics and could write.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from the Song dynasty top graduate Zhou Tan. His father Richeng was a classical scholar and a capable writer.

sentences.zh: 海賊竊據溫州，拘日成置海舟上，樂隨往，事其父甚謹。

translations.literal: Sea bandits seized and held Wenzhou, detained Richeng and placed him on a sea vessel; Le followed along and served his father with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates seized Wenzhou, took Richeng aboard a ship at sea, and Le went with him, tending his father with meticulous care.

sentences.zh: 一日賊酋遣人沉日成於水，樂泣請曰：「我有祖母，幸留父侍養，請以己代父死。

translations.literal: One day the bandit chief sent someone to sink Richeng in the water; Le wept and requested: "I have a grandmother—please leave my father to support her; please let me die in my father's stead.
translations.idiomatic: One day the chief ordered Richeng thrown overboard. Le wept and begged: "I still have a grandmother at home. Let my father live to care for her—take my life instead.

sentences.zh: 」不聽，樂抱父不忍舍，遂同死焉。

translations.literal: " They would not listen; Le embraced his father and could not bear to release him, and thus died together.
translations.idiomatic: " They refused. Le clung to his father and would not let go, and both drowned.
